    How to Use the Random Order Generator

    Type or paste your list, one item per line, from 2 to 500 items. Tap Shuffle and you get the whole list back in a random, numbered order. Shuffle again gives a fresh order from the same list, and Copy order copies it with the numbers, ready to paste into a chat or a doc.

    What happens to your list

    Every item shows up exactly once. Nothing is dropped and nothing is added. Blank lines are skipped. If you typed the same thing on two lines, it stays in twice, on the assumption you meant it.

    The shuffle is a Fisher–Yates shuffle using your browser's secure random number generator, so every possible order is equally likely and the first item on your list has no better chance of going first. It all happens on your device. Nothing is uploaded or saved.

    Ways to use it

    • Presentation order. Class presentations, standups, demo day.
    • Turn order. Board games, draft picks, who goes first at karaoke.
    • Auditions and tryouts. A running order nobody can say was rigged.
    • Playlists. Paste the song titles and get a fresh order.
    • Chores. Shuffle the jobs, then hand them out in order.

    Frequently Asked Questions

    Is the order really random?

    Yes. It's a Fisher–Yates shuffle, the standard method for this, using your browser's secure random number generator. Every possible order is equally likely.

    Does every item appear once?

    Yes. The output has exactly the items you put in, each once. If you typed something twice, it appears twice, because each line is its own item.

    What happens to blank lines?

    They're ignored. So are spaces at the start and end of a line.

    How many items can I shuffle?

    From 2 to 500.

    Is my list uploaded anywhere?

    No. The shuffle runs in your browser and nothing is saved or sent anywhere.
